positioning: The bald extrovert. A warm, wrinkled lapcat that acts more like a clingy toddler.
story: The Sphynx looks engineered in a lab, but it is an accident of nature. The breed traces to a hairless kitten born in Toronto in 1966, and breeders worked to build a healthy line around that single mutation. The result is a cat that is famous for what it does not have.

It is not truly hairless. A Sphynx is covered in a fine down like the skin of a peach, warm and soft to the touch, with a body heat you feel at once. Big bat ears, a wrinkled face, and large lemon-shaped eyes give it a look that people either adore or find startling.

That bare skin needs care. Without a coat to absorb them, skin oils build up, so a Sphynx needs regular bathing and warm spots to curl into. It feels the cold and will burrow under blankets or against your neck.

The personality is the real reason for its rise. The Sphynx is an attention-seeking extrovert, energetic, clownish, and relentlessly affectionate, the cat most likely to greet your guests and supervise your every move. It is often called the most dog-like cat of all.

A Sphynx is high-maintenance in surprising ways. With no coat to absorb them, skin oils build up and leave a waxy film, so most need a wipe-down or a bath every week or two, along with regular ear and nail cleaning. They burn energy fast and feel the cold, so they seek out sweaters, sunbeams, and laps.

In temperament it is pure extrovert, demanding, comic, and devoted, the cat most likely to wake you for attention and least happy left alone. The breed can carry the heart condition HCM and a skin and gum disorder, so good breeders screen, and the cat needs warmth, calories, and company to thrive.
fblocks: Named for its resemblance to the bald, ancient look of Egyptian sphinx statues, though the breed is modern and Canadian.
The breed grew from a single hairless kitten born in Toronto in 1966, bred carefully for health.
It needs warmth, regular bathing to manage skin oils, and lots of company. It is not hypoallergenic, since it still produces the usual cat allergen.
Effectively bald, with a soft peach-fuzz down and visible skin in many colors and patterns, often wrinkled around the face.
Among the most recognizable cats in the world and a steady presence near the top of CFA registrations.
Bathe regularly, keep it warm, and never leave it lonely. The Sphynx is needy, playful, and endlessly involved in your day.
Can carry the heart condition HCM. Wipe the skin to manage oils, clean the ears often, and choose screened breeders.
days: The Sphynx is not hairless. It wears a fine down, as soft as a peach.
The breed began with one hairless kitten born in Toronto in 1966.
The name nods to Egyptian statues, but the Sphynx is a modern Canadian cat.
Warm skin, a knitted blanket, and no plans. The Sphynx knows where the heat is.
A cold window is for looking. A warm bed is for living. Choose wisely.
Ask who greeted the guests and supervised the unpacking. The Sphynx did.
An elder Sphynx in a nest of wool. Still the warmest thing in the house.
last_walk:
Snow outside, wool all around, and one cream cat settled at last.
The Sphynx has followed you from room to room all week and kept every lap warm. Now it sits on the quilt by the window, eyes half closed, a small heater with ears. Tomorrow it will want company again.
cap: The famous hairless cat, a fixture of CFA's top fifteen
